gap: No result ChatGPT got states cost per usable watt-hour from one reviewer's measured efficiency: with The Solar Lab's figures the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (94%) costs 46.1¢ per usable Wh at $899 (43.8¢ at $854.05 with code) against 54.3¢ for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max (79%) at $879, which reverses their order on rated $/Wh (43.4¢ vs 42.9¢).
standout_why: Compared against outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000 (cited), outagereadyhq.com under-1000, thewattlist.com, powerreserveguide.com and PopSci's Black Friday roundup (cited). Outageoutfitter gives rated $ per kWh only ($434 Elite 200 V2, $429 DELTA 3 Max) and one identical '1.6 days' fridge figure for all five units. Outagereadyhq gives $/Wh and hours at 120 W, but from an assumed 85% for every unit. Thewattlist, powerreserveguide and PopSci state no per-Wh, per-lb, idle or measured-efficiency figure. None has Wh per lb, idle loss per day, or cost per measured usable Wh. ChatGPT's own answers used a flat 85% and '17 hours at 100 W' for both units; chat 2 did quote Popular Mechanics' 92% for the Bluetti, so the measured-efficiency idea is partly present. Business Insider, Popular Mechanics and Car and Driver refused the fetch, so they are not compared.
decides: It settles Elite 200 V2 against DELTA 3 Max, the two units ChatGPT picked in its two answers: the Bluetti delivers about 331 more usable Wh (1,949 vs 1,618), about 3.3 more hours at 100 W, and loses 228 Wh a day to idle against 648 Wh. The EcoFlow's 8.6 lb weight advantage disappears on usable Wh per lb (36.2 vs 36.5). It does not settle #1: the DJI Power 2000 (84%) beats the Elite's 43.8¢ per usable Wh at any price under about $754, and I could not read DJI's price today; the desk lead of $679.99 would give 39.5¢ if another agent confirms it. The Pecron F3000LFP at $899 (pre-order, ships mid-December) is cheapest per rated Wh at 29.3¢ and would need to measure below about 67% to lose to the Elite per usable Wh, but I found no Solar Lab measurement for it. So the finding confirms the Elite 200 V2 ahead of the DELTA 3 Max and is consistent with the desk placement (DJI #1 if its price is verified, Pecron and Elite next).

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 94% efficiency; 9.5 W idle
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab says it bought the unit itself and calls 94% the highest it has recorded. Test load and review date are not stated on the page. Its spec list gives 53.4 lb and 2,073 Wh.

findings.label: Usable Wh and hours at 100 W
findings.value: 1,949 Wh usable; 19.5 h at 100 W
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 2,073.6 Wh (BLUETTI's figure, from Dealectric's record) × 0.94 = 1,949.2 Wh; ÷ 100 W = 19.5 h. ChatGPT said about 17 h from an assumed 85%.

findings.label: Cost per usable Wh
findings.value: 46.1¢ at $899 store price; 43.8¢ at $854.05 with code
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: $899 ÷ 1,949.2 Wh = $0.461; $854.05 ÷ 1,949.2 Wh = $0.438. Per rated Wh: $899 ÷ 2,073.6 = 43.4¢; $854.05 ÷ 2,073.6 = 41.2¢. Prices are Dealectric's record (store page read 2026-11-27, cart test 2026-11-26), used as given; I did not re-open the BLUETTI page (my guessed product URL returned 404 and the store search listed only bundles). Sale ends Nov 30; ships early January 2027 per the desk notes.

findings.label: Idle loss per day and idle days
findings.value: 228 Wh per 24 h (11.0% of capacity); 9.1 days to empty with nothing plugged in
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 9.5 W × 24 h = 228 Wh; 228 ÷ 2,073.6 = 11.0%; 2,073.6 Wh ÷ 9.5 W ÷ 24 = 9.1 days. The review does not say whether the AC outlets were on for the idle reading.

findings.label: Wh per lb (rated and usable)
findings.value: 38.8 Wh/lb rated; 36.5 usable Wh/lb
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 2,073.6 ÷ 53.4 lb = 38.8; 1,949.2 ÷ 53.4 = 36.5. Weight is from The Solar Lab's spec list (outageoutfitter.com also prints 53.4 lb); the maker's page was not opened.

findings.label: Continuous watts per dollar
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review: A Solid Comeback? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 2,600 W ÷ $899 = 2.89; 2,600 W ÷ $854.05 = 3.04. The Solar Lab lists the 2,600 W inverter; prices as in Dealectric's record.

findings.label: Price, weight and recharge (maker)

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'came in at 79%'; idle about 27 W, 'roughly three days'. Test load and review date not stated. It reports 68 min as 0–100%; EcoFlow's own page says 68 min is 0–80%.

findings.value: 1,618 Wh usable; 16.2 h at 100 W
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 2,048 Wh × 0.79 = 1,617.9 Wh; ÷ 100 W = 16.2 h. That is 331 Wh and 3.3 h less than the Elite 200 V2 on the same reviewer's figures.

findings.label: Cost per usable Wh
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Portable Power Station (2048Wh), EcoFlow US
findings.note: $879 ÷ 1,617.9 Wh = $0.543. Per rated Wh: $879 ÷ 2,048 = 42.9¢, which is below the Elite's 43.4¢ at $899, so the order reverses once measured efficiency is applied.

findings.label: Idle loss per day and idle days
findings.value: 648 Wh per 24 h (31.6% of capacity); 3.2 days to empty with nothing plugged in

findings.note: 27 W × 24 h = 648 Wh; 648 ÷ 2,048 = 31.6%; 2,048 ÷ 27 ÷ 24 = 3.2 days, matching The Solar Lab's 'roughly three days'.

findings.label: Measured efficiency, idle draw and derived figures (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 89% efficiency; about 18 W idle; 1,823 Wh usable; 18.2 h at 100 W; 432 Wh idle per 24 h (21.1%); 48.8 Wh/lb rated, 43.4 usable Wh/lb

findings.note: 2,048 × 0.89 = 1,822.7 Wh; ÷ 100 = 18.2 h; 18 × 24 = 432 Wh; 2,048 ÷ 42 lb = 48.8; 1,822.7 ÷ 42 = 43.4. Weight 42 lb and 88 min 0–100% wall recharge are The Solar Lab's figures. Break-even against the Elite's 43.8¢: 1,822.7 × $0.4382 = $798.7. No price read today.
